newsitem.title: UK: Ex-owners compete for bankrupt German Beta refinery.
newsitem.headline: Ex-owners compete for bankrupt German Beta refinery.

text.p: Germany's bankrupt Beta refinery in Wilhelmshaven has received competing bids from the two previous co-owners who fell out last year, sending the plant into receivership, industry sources said on Thursday.
Bidding has now closed and the official receiver for the 190,000 barrel a day (bpd) plant is expected to announce a decision on the winning bid by the end of January.
Industry sources said the two bids were submitted by SA Louis Dreyfus CIE of France and Bulk Oil AG of Switzerland.
Bulk Oil AG has the same majority shareholders as Beta's previous co-owner Holding Tusculum BV, industry sources familar with the companies say.
The bids are believed to value the refinery at about $60 million.
Beta's future was thrown into doubt last year after dispute between shareholders SA Louis Dreyfus CIE and Holding Tusculum last year.
SA Louis Dreyfus CIE has invested over $200 million in the north Germam refinery and enjoyed improved profit margins at the refinery last year, industry sources said.
The company's London trading subsdiary extended an agreement to process crude oil at the refinery until April 3, 1997.
The export refinery has low operating costs but faces a tough outlook in Europe where refineries have been labouring under the burden of some 600,000 to one million bpd of excess capacity for years.

Nevertheless, Wilhelmshaven has successfully carved out a niche market selling low sulphur oil products into Scandinavia. Its profitability largely depends on exporting refined oil products into the volatile international spot market.
